reuse.why: The change extends the existing category predicate and reuses spending selection, amount conversion, tag extraction, batching, and undo abstractions.

duplication.why: Eligibility decisions remain shared, although the category metadata projection and joins are repeated across three queries.

placement.why: Budget policy stays in server budget actions, tag parsing stays shared, and method registration follows the existing application layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their registration, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: The shared predicate and options type make future policy changes straightforward, with minor maintenance friction from repeated query metadata and the average-specific name of the reused amount helper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All affected month-wide actions use isMonthFillCategory, and setLastMonthSpending also uses the shared spending selection and amount conversion helpers.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated SQL metadata is explicit; the new consumer shares eligibility and sign conversion rather than reshaping those decisions locally.

abstraction_drift.where: getSpendingFillCategories gains the requested hidden-category parameter; isMonthFillCategory renames its existing flag and adds universal exclusions without consumer-specific branches or bypasses.
